newsitem.title: USA: Dynatronics buys treatment table assets.
newsitem.headline: Dynatronics buys treatment table assets.

text.p: Dynatronics Corp said on Tuesday it had acquired assets to begin manufacturing physical therapy treatment tables, parallel bars, and other specialty rehabilitation treatment tables at a facility in Columbia, South Carolina. The purchase price was not disclosed.

Dynatronics signed a deal with Charlton "Stoney" Floyd, the president of Midland Table Co, to purchase inventory and equipment, and lease real and personal property owned by Floyd, Dynatronics said. Sammons Preston owns Midland Table.
Floyd has agreed to act as general manager of the facility, which generates $3 million in revenues annually.
Dynatronics said it plans to introduce new products related to treatment tables and that its company sales should increase by 10 to 20 percent when its products are fully developed.

Dynatronics's new products should be out in three to six months, Bob Cardon, the company's corporate secretary, said. Cardon said the company reported fiscal year sales of $6.7 million for the year ended June 1996 and that figure is expected to rise by 50 percent for the year ended June 1997, Cardon said.
